finding.claim: update_doc calls can_edit() but ignores its boolean result (should be require_edit), so any authenticated user can overwrite the body of any document regardless of ownership or editor status.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (g.user) sending PUT /doc/<doc_id> with JSON body, choosing an arbitrary doc_id
finding.sink: doc["body"] = request.json["body"] at docs.py:20 (modification of a protected document)

trace.note: doc = DOCS[doc_id] fetched with no owner scoping
can_edit(g.user, doc) returns bool, result discarded, no abort

finding.guards_checked: can_edit at line 19 is the only guard and its return value is unused; the sibling route update_title correctly uses require_edit (line 27) which aborts 403, confirming the intended control is missing here. No other auth decorator or before_request hook exists in the file.

verdict.guard_found: can_edit at docs.py:19 is called as a bare statement, so its bool result is discarded. require_edit (docs.py:11-13) aborts with 403 but is not called in update_doc. No before_request hook or auth decorator exists in the directory.
verdict.reason: docs.py:19 calls can_edit() (docs.py:7-8, returns a bool) without testing the result, so docs.py:20 overwrites the body for any user, unlike update_title which calls require_edit at docs.py:27.
